AltschulerBoixAdsera2023StructuredMOT: scalar linear-cost dual certificates and sparse recovery, not a tie-safe spectral minimax certificate with distinct algebraic and rational interfaces.

RaoZhang2025DDM gives an unequal-margin MWU upper guarantee; AltschulerBoixAdsera2023StructuredMOT gives exact sparse MOT for one fixed linear cost. Neither states the proposed fixed-row spectral Bellman certificate and rational recovery result.
Haus2015Mixability enumerates fixed-row states and AltschulerBoixAdsera2023StructuredMOT uses pricing oracles; neither gives certified pruning for the changing PSD spectral direction.

AltschulerBoixAdsera2023StructuredMOT gives sparse MOT vertices and HarmanEtAl2024OptimalDesignPolytope studies optimal-design polytopes; the stated feature-rank count is a specialized support-compression component.
HarshawSavjeSpielmanZhang2024GSW and RaoZhang2025DDM provide the covariance-to-Horvitz--Thompson-risk bridge for linear outcome classes.
The block-zero covariance identity is elementary linear algebra; the source-preserving adapter is a useful benchmark component rather than an independent research kernel.
No named paper supplies this exact empirical-law repair formula, but it is a direct mixture construction rather than a standalone novelty claim.
No inspected comparator exhibits this stated rational unequal-margin irrational spectral optimum with a local certificate.

novelty_flags.one_line: These fields attribute a factor (1+epsilon) to Rao--Zhang Theorem 4.2, but the proceedings theorem states (1+epsilon)^2.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: For epsilon in (0,1), the theorem gives f_B(D) <= (1+epsilon)^2 min{f_B(D_Bernoulli), 1+1/epsilon}, with runtime polynomial in m, n, and epsilon^{-1}.
Theorem 4.1 equates tractability of ELLIPSOID, MOT, and MIN; Theorem 4.3 returns an optimal sparse vertex using polynomially many ARGMIN calls.
The paper states that complete mixability can be solved by dynamic programming in pseudopolynomial time for a fixed number of rows.

source_verification_receipts.version: Journal of the American Statistical Association 119(548), 2024
source_verification_receipts.locator: article abstract and stated Theorems 4.5 and 6.4
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The article relates covariance control under the Gram--Schmidt walk to finite-sample Horvitz--Thompson mean-squared-error control for linear outcome structure.
The exact symbolic SDP method has polynomial complexity when either the number of variables or matrix size is fixed; it does not provide the proposed pathwise Bellman certificate.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Replace every occurrence of the Rao--Zhang guarantee by the exact proceedings formula with factor (1+epsilon)^2, and retain the narrower claim that the proposal strengthens certification information on the fixed-row class.

State the comparative theorem as a formally checkable separation: same normalized objective and input class, Rao--Zhang upper-only output versus an additive instance-optimal interval with exact marginals and a verifier; include a worked nontrivial certificate instance.

If aiming above field tier, add a second published experimental-design comparator and a theorem establishing a frontier over a generic class of certificate-producing designs, rather than only a single-comparator certification improvement.

recommended_next_step: Correct the Rao--Zhang Theorem 4.2 factor everywhere, then continue to Stage 0 with the field-tier fixed-row certificate kernel.
